identification: Five common two-tone salt-glazed stoneware pieces: four cylindrical storage jars (three tan/cream, one all cream) and a one-gallon style tan-top demijohn with strap handle. Photos show a bead-moulded band on one jar and a faint oval impressed mark on the shoulder of another; no legible maker. Typical Australian/English domestic and trade jars, c.1900-1950. Value is as a decorative lot, not individual maker pieces unless the mark proves to be Bendigo, McHugh, Fowler or similar.

viewing_check: Photograph the oval impressed mark on the shoulder of the jar in photo 1 (left) and the faint demijohn mark under raking light to see if it reads Bendigo, McHugh, Fowler, Doulton, Lovatt or similar; check bases for stamps; check rims and demijohn spout and handle for chips and hairlines.
